subject: ClearPath reference wiring: control->data handoff for private deployments
messages:
From: AeroTech <stephanie@aerotech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearPath kickoff — control/data wiring questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the kickoff earlier. Before we lock the cutover window, I wanted to confirm one operational detail: how will control-plane management calls (provisioning, model pinning, rollback) be routed across the customer VPC boundary to Redwood's control plane in the private deployment pattern we discussed?

Specifically: if we host the data-plane in our colo and use the private control-plane appliance in our VPC, are management calls proxied through an egress gateway, or are they TLS connections directly to the control-plane endpoint? We need this to satisfy our change board and NAC rules.

Also attaching the network baseline from our side (small stub). Happy to hop on a short call.

Regards,
Stephanie
Head of Cloud Ops, AeroTech

Attachments: aerotech-network-baseline.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: AeroTech <stephanie@aerotech.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ClearPath kickoff — control/data wiring questions

Hi Stephanie — thanks for the detailed note and the baseline. Short answer: the recommended pattern is TLS direct to a customer-scoped control-plane endpoint (mutual TLS), with an optional authenticated egress relay when customers require a single outbound proxy.

Key bullets so we have the same expectations:
- Control-plane (management) traffic: mTLS to control-plane endpoint (port 443) pinned to customer certs; requires inbound rule on the control-plane appliance side.
- Data-plane (inference) traffic: stays within the colo cluster; outbound requests to external model artifacts (if any) go through the egress gateway by policy.
- Optional relay: for customers that mandate outbound-only connectivity, we provide a signed relay proxy pattern (short-lived tunnels + tokenized control channel).

I'm attaching a short "reference wiring" PDF that maps the control -> data handoff and the recommended firewall rules. Jonas, Mateo — can you confirm the routing table snippets and the proposed canary cutover steps (we'll want a tiny subset of tenants for the first week)?

Thanks,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: clearpath-wiring-diagram-v1.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

On Thu, Aug 16, 2028 at 10:05 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Stephanie — thanks for the detailed note and the baseline. Short answer: the recommended pattern is TLS direct to a customer-scoped control-plane endpoint (mutual TLS), with an optional authenticated egress relay when customers require a single outbound proxy.

Thanks Marissa — adding a couple of operational clarifications here that AeroTech asked for during the call:

1) BGP / IP expectations: if the control-plane appliance is assigned a customer VPC address, control-plane health checks and model-manager callbacks will originate from those IPs. We will publish an expected IP range for the handoff and also support an FQDN that resolves to the appliance for customers that don't allow IP whitelisting.

2) Canary plan (proposed):
- Day 0: deploy control-plane appliance in staging (customer VPC) with canary certs.
- Day 1: route 2% of tenant traffic (shadow inference) to the new data-plane config; metrics-only (no billing).
- Day 3: 10% traffic, enable model pinning.
- Day 7: full cutover if no regressions.

3) Observability hooks: we will emit per-tenant traces for control-plane calls and a short TTL log retention policy for the canary window (30 days) to limit PII exposure.

Mateo — I've attached a short playbook with the exact iptables/ACL snippets and the canary cutover checklist. Stephanie — let me know if you want us to wire a brief runbook call with your SREs.

Jonas
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

Attachments: clearpath-canary-playbook.md (attachment stub)

From: Stephanie AeroTech <stephanie@aerotech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: ClearPath reference wiring: control->data handoff for private deployments

Thanks all — this is helpful and maps to our security board checklist. A few quick answers and next steps:

- We prefer the FQDN approach rather than IP whitelisting; please provide the DNS entries and cert details.
- We'll schedule a 30-minute runbook call on Monday (Aug 20) to walk the SREs through the playbook and ACL snippets.
- For the canary, AeroTech will start with a single internal tenant (non-production) and move to 10% after Day 2. We also need a short-living escalation contact for the cutover window.

Can you provide the DNS name you want us to use for the appliance and the CSR procedure for the mTLS certs? Also please share the Drive folder link you referenced so our reviewers can see the diagrams.

Appreciate the responsiveness — looking forward to the call.

– Stephanie
Head of Cloud Ops, AeroTech
